sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Public Commercial Web Scraping and Proxy API Gateways

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law — governed by the Luxembourg Civil Code, the Luxembourg Commercial Code, and the consolidated Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as modernized by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the SCSp)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — freedom of establishment (Article 49), free movement of services (Article 56) and capital (Article 63)
Luxembourg–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (DTA) of 1996, as amended by the Protocols of 2004 and 2009
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) network of more than 90 bilateral investment treaties in force with capital-exporting and capital-importing states
BLEU–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2005, in force 2009)
Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Hague Apostille Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended; transposing EU Directive 2015/849, Directive 2018/843 and Directive 2018/1673); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (SCSp framework per the Law of 23 July 2016); FATF Recommendations as applied by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier — CRF)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (LBR-RBE) is not fully public; access is confined to (i) competent authorities (CRF, CSSF, judicial and prosecutorial authorities), (ii) AML/CFT obliged entities under the Law of 2004, and (iii) any person demonstrating a legitimate interest; public access was further restricted following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022 (WM and Sovim SA)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / commercial register extract of each corporate partner (including any corporate general partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company register / registrar in the country of origin of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the country of origin (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified board resolutions and signing-authority extracts of each corporate partner authorizing the establishment of the SCSp and the signing of the partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered directors / company secretary of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of all beneficial owners, the general partner(s) (if individuals) and all authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin / competent national passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill, bank statement or official administrative certificate) for each individual UBO and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider / credit institution / municipal administration of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with certified French/English translation, plus Hague Apostille where required by the receiving Luxembourg AML obligé

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate of each corporate partner (supporting the pass-through tax classification and treaty eligibility)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax administration of each partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states); English or French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC questionnaire, PEP declaration, and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth declarations for all UBOs and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg AML compliance provider / Luxembourg counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signatures of declarants; internal professional document not requiring apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Incorporation deed or official registration excerpt of any corporate partner formed more than six months prior to filing (fresh-certificate rule)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register of the jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004, Article 3(5)-(6): (i) initial and ongoing screening of all UBOs, general partner(s), managers and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg CRF targeted financial sanctions database, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and related restrictive-measure regulations), the UN Security Council consolidated list, and — because the target payment rails are Stripe and Circle USDC — the OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions list, including on-chain screening of every USDC wallet address against OFAC sanctioned-address databases; (ii) determination of PEP status and close-associate relationships for every individual, with mandatory senior-approval and source-of-wealth verification for any PEP; (iii) substantive verification of source of funds and source of wealth for all contributed capital and future distributions; (iv) negative-media and global sanctions-registry monitoring conducted at onboarding, on each material change, and at least annually; (v) the SCSp's own activity (ISIC 6201 — commercial web scraping and proxy API) is not a regulated financial activity, so the entity acts as a client of Luxembourg AML obligés (notary, bank, PSP); nevertheless the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier requires contractual acceptance of CRF/OFC-style reporting duties and the appointment of a compliance contact person in Luxembourg.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg, operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); filings are made exclusively through the eJustice portal (www.ejustice.lu); public name search and status verification available at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the primary statutory filing language; the registered name must be expressed in Latin-script characters; any non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the RCS filing; the SCSp name must include the legal suffix 'SCSp' or the full form 'Société en commandite spéciale'; the name may otherwise be in French, German, English or another Latin-script language provided it is not misleading, does not conflict with an existing RCS entry, and is reproducible in the partnership agreement, letterhead, invoices and online gateways in exactly the registered form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: There is no statutory extension of the 30-day reservation; re-reservation for successive 30-day windows is required. Procedural SOP upon rejection: (1) obtain the written statutory ground from the LBR Guichet Unique via eJustice; (2) re-file immediately with a modified, distinguishable name at no additional statutory fee; (3) if rejection rests on a sensitive token (e.g., 'Banque' or 'Fonds'), obtain the prior written authorization of the Minister of Justice, with the advisory opinion of the CSSF or the Ministère des Finances where the token implicates the financial sector, before re-submission; (4) alternatively, lodge a formal administrative appeal ('recours en réformation') before the Tribunal administratif of Luxembourg within three months of the refusal; a pending appeal does not suspend the rights of a prior registrant, so parallel reservation of a fallback name is recommended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional acceptance: a Luxembourg SCSp may use the address of a licensed professional domiciliation agent to satisfy RCS formalities, but genuine commercial substance is required — a physical office, local management meetings, locally available accounting records and, where the structure permits, a Luxembourg-resident general partner — in order to secure Luxembourg tax-residence treatment under the Law of 10 August 1915, to satisfy the ATAD/general anti-abuse rules and the OECD BEPS nexus approach, and to pass bank, Stripe and PSP underwriting. A pure virtual-office arrangement is deemed insufficient for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and would elevate audit and substance-challenge risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 12-15% cumulative probability of a substance or audit verification by the Administration des contributions directes over a three-year cycle; less than 5% annual probability of an RCS compliance check, triggered generally by material inconsistencies in registry filings; near-zero probability of unannounced inspection by the AML/CFT supervisor so long as the entity does not hold a VASP or financial-services authorization. The likelihood rises to approximately 25-30% where a virtual office is combined with fully non-resident management.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory name availability search and reservation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of approximately EUR 30 per name reservation under the LBR/eJustice fee schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; special limited partnership provisions of Articles 904-1 to 904-14 (inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and on the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership agreement (contrat de société) filed with the RCS and the corresponding extract (extrait du RCS) after registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; capital is set entirely in the partnership agreement. Contributions may be made in cash, in kind, or in industry. No escrow account is mandatory under Luxembourg law; escrow may be agreed contractually for closing mechanics or if the SCSp is authorised as an AIF and subject to AIFMD rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution of the General Partner of the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) adopted on [date] by written consent of all directors. RESOLVED: (1) The subscriptions to partnership interests by the initial limited partners, as set out in the partnership agreement, are hereby approved and accepted. (2) The registered office is fixed at [registered address], Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg). (3) [Name] is appointed the manager (gérant) of the SCSp, with full power to open bank accounts, execute filings, and represent the partnership before authorities. (4) The manager or any authorized director is instructed to file this resolution and the partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and arrange RESA publication. (5) This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All partners (general partner and initial limited partners); a notary public of Luxembourg if notarisation is preferred
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the SCSp partnership agreement containing the name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate object (public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways), contribution amounts, profit and loss sharing, management rights of the general partner, and dissolution terms. The agreement may be concluded by private deed or by notarial act; if private deed, ensure each partner's signature is authenticated for RCS e-filing purposes. The name must include the words 'société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Identity documents (passport or national ID) of each partner
Proof of the registered office address in Luxembourg (lease agreement or ownership deed)
Optional name reservation certificate from the RCS
Declaration of good repute for each manager/general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or notary raises a query on the deed, amend the deed by an addendum or by execution of a corrective deed and re-submit; refund of notary fees may be negotiable if the deed is rejected before notarisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Online e-filing portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the LBR electronic filing service, complete the standard constitution form F-01, attach the signed partnership agreement and all relevant supporting documents, and pay the online filing fee. The RCS will verify the uniqueness of the company name and the compliance of the deed, then issue the certificate of registration (extrait du RCS). The SCSp obtains legal standing for trade and administrative relations only after this registration.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form F-01
Partnership agreement (original or certified true copy)
Name reservation certificate, if applicable
Identity documents of all partners and the manager
Proof of registered office address
Statutory declaration of acceptance by each manager/general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the RCS will suspend the process and request corrections or missing documents. Respond within 15 days through the online portal; otherwise the file is closed and fees may be partially refunded. Once the query is resolved, registration is completed within two working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA official electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after RCS registration, the RCS forwards the deed to RESA for publication. Verify that the published excerpt contains the SCSp name, legal form, registered office, object, duration, manager details, and any capital disclosures. The publication is performed electronically and is free of charge as part of the initial filing fee.
required_dossiers: RCS registration receipt
Extract of the registered partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the LBR support with the RCS registration number and filing date; request the electronic publication to be issued within one additional working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Luxembourg business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (General Directorate of Middle Classes), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the SCSp carries on a commercial activity, it must hold a general establishment permit even though the underlying data-scraping and API-gateway business is not a regulated profession. File the electronic application with proof of RCS registration, evidence of good repute and professional capacity of the manager, and the effective commercial establishment. The permit is issued under the law of 2 September 2011 on access to crafts, trades, and professions.
required_dossiers: Application form for autorisation d'établissement
RCS extract issued within the last three months
Criminal record extracts for each manager
Proof of professional indemnity insurance, if applicable
Evidence of registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing within ten working days providing the requested clarifications. If the permit is refused, an appeal may be filed with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months from notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final filing verification and distribution of corporate due-diligence package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS company extracts online service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration and RESA publication, log in to the LBR portal and download the final certified RCS excerpt in French or German. Assemble the complete corporate package (extract, partnership agreement, RESA excerpt, and establishment permit) for use in banking and payment processor due diligence, including Stripe and cryptocurrency payment settlements.
required_dossiers: Updated RCS extract
Published partnership agreement from RESA
Establishment permit (if issued)
Identity document of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If data in the extract is incorrect, submit a correction request to the RCS through the online portal with the supporting deed; the corrected extract is issued within two working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (General Directorate of Middle Classes), Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No regulated industrial operating permit is applicable to pure software/data-API services; a general business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) is covered under Step 4.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a digital data service with no substantial physical installation, no stationary combustion source, no wastewater, and no hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no VOC or particulate emission thresholds are engaged. IT hardware disposal shall follow the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU through certified recyclers. Data-centre energy consumption is monitored indirectly through Scope 2 GHG reporting if the entity voluntarily adopts the GHG Protocol.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of the commercial office space is required only if the workforce exceeds 100 persons or the building is classified with high fire load. Structural load inspection is dispensed for standard office occupancy. The SCSp must complete the workplace registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and, before occupancy, post evacuation plans and provide a first-aid kit. Occupational health and safety clearance is obtained through the ITM declaration for the office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate and personal income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and indirect taxes. Official portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.public.lu; electronic filing via eCDF (ACD) and e-TVA (AEDT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities and SCSp partnerships without a Luxembourg seat must obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number before effecting their first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Procedure: (1) Confirm whether the SCSp creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment; for direct-tax purposes the fiscally transparent SCSp requires no entity-level corporate tax registration, as income is taxed at partner level. (2) Submit VAT Form 106 (demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) to the AEDT either directly via MyGuichet.lu or through a Luxembourg fiscal representative (mandatory for non-EU principals; optional for EU principals). (3) Provide the SCSp partnership deed (notarized or apostilled extract), identity and residence evidence of the general partner and limited partners, service contracts and API gateway agreements, hosting or proxy-server infrastructure documents showing Luxembourg nexus, certificate of foreign tax registration, and VIES confirmation where applicable. (4) Upon approval the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT number in the format 'LU' plus 8 digits; a 15-digit national identification number (matricule) may be issued through the Luxembourg Business Registers if a local establishment is created. (5) Invoicing may not legally precede VAT registration; late registration triggers fines under Article 63 LVT of EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 plus monthly late interest of 0.8%.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is a contract-type special limited partnership without legal personality under the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915, as amended. Under Article 184 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR), the SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent: no corporate income tax, no municipal business tax, and no net-wealth tax arise at the entity level. Each partner (general or limited) is taxed individually on their allocable share of partnership income; foreign partners are then subject to the territorial and residence rules of their home jurisdiction. The SCSp therefore does not appear as a separate taxpayer on the Luxembourg direct-tax register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no statutory check-the-box election comparable to US Federal Form 8832; SCSp transparency is a mandatory legal default under Article 184 LIR. Available elections and instruments are: (i) drafting the partnership agreement with flexible profit and loss allocations, subject to economic-substance review and the general anti-abuse provision under Article 6 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (AStG); (ii) applying for an advance tax ruling from the ACD to confirm entity classification, permanent-establishment treatment and anti-hybrid outcomes binding on the tax authorities; (iii) electing symmetrical treatment for hybrid entities under ATAD I and II (Articles 168ter et seq. LIR) so as to eliminate double non-taxation or double deduction mismatches; (iv) for US partners, making a US check-the-box election to treat the SCSp as an association taxable as a corporation — such election creates a hybrid entity whose Luxembourg tax consequences must then be neutralized under the anti-hybrid rules unless the partners make offsetting deemed-payment adjustments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended (Loi sur la TVA, LVT), implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established suppliers: EUR 0 — no monetary threshold; VAT registration is immediately triggered by any taxable supply made in Luxembourg. Luxembourg-established small businesses: annual turnover exemption up to EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT), with compulsory registration thereafter. Cross-border B2C distance sales of e-services within the EU: EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual threshold; below this threshold Luxembourg VAT applies, above it registration or the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme in the customer's EU Member State becomes mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC), no mandatory digital stamping, and no Italian-style clearance system apply in Luxembourg as of 2025. Mandatory electronic invoicing applies exclusively to business-to-government (B2G) supplies via the PEPPOL network and UBL/BIS 3.0 structured formats, pursuant to the Grand-Ducal Regulation implementing EU Directive 2014/55/EU. B2B e-invoicing remains optional and may use PDF, Factur-X/ZUGFeRD, or UN/EDIFACT formats. Invoices must be archived for 10 years; OSS-return documentation and customer-location evidence (IP addresses, bank details, country of establishment certificates, SIM cards, billing addresses) must also be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For the relevant digital services (public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways): B2B supplies to non-EU established customers are taxable at the customer's place of business under the general place-of-supply rule, giving an effective Luxembourg VAT rate of 0% with the customer self-assessing any local VAT. B2B supplies to EU customers are reverse-charged to the recipient (Article 58 LVT) and are likewise outside Luxembourg VAT. B2C e-services to non-EU consumers fall outside Luxembourg's territorial scope. Physical export of goods (e.g., server hardware or media embodying the API service) qualifies for the 0% export rate under Article 42 LVT provided dispatch or transport to a third-country destination is completed within 90 days of despatch and evidenced; intra-Community supplies require the customer's valid EU VAT number and listing in the recapitulative statement. In all cases, the supplier must retain complete documentary proof of delivery, identity of the recipient, and actual payment for at least 10 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (single administrative document / EAD) — required only for physical goods, not for purely digital API services
Bill of Lading / CMR / air waybill evidencing transport to the third-country destination, where physical hardware or media is exported
Commercial invoice expressly marked 'Export zero-rated under Article 42 LVT' or 'Reverse charge — Article 58 LVT'
Executed master service agreement or API licensing contract identifying the foreign customer and confirming their business establishment
Foreign customer's VAT registration certificate or equivalent tax-residency certificate proving B2B status and place of establishment
VIES validation output for EU intra-Community customers
IP-geolocation logs, server-trace evidence and payment-rail data (Stripe records, USDC on-chain transaction hashes) substantiating the recipient's actual location for e-services
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank credit advice evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from the foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess zero-rated or non-established supplies within the standard 5-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud, falsified documents or abusive arrangements. On challenge, the full 17% Luxembourg VAT becomes due together with late-payment interest of 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum). Administrative fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 per invoice under Article 63 LVT; where the exporter knowingly submits forged export evidence or conceals the real recipient, criminal fines up to double the evaded tax and imprisonment may apply under Article 64 LVT. Partner and general-manager joint-and-several liability can further attach under Luxembourg anti-abuse principles where the data-pipeline services are routed through an artificial structure to disguise the true exporter or beneficiary. Payment received materially later than 180 days may be treated as evidence of a rescinded sale, supporting denial of the zero rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in close coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) under the Eurosystem; cross-border capital movement oversight is additionally governed by the CSSF for financial-sector participants and by EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both capital and current account transactions throughout Luxembourg. There are no statutory exchange controls, no prior-authorisation duties for profit remittances, and no restrictions on incoming direct investment. Dividends or profit shares paid by a taxable Luxembourg entity are subject to potential Luxembourg withholding tax, but SCSp tax-transparent vehicles are not themselves subject to withholding at entity level; foreign partners are taxed according to their own residence status. The only practical hurdles arise from EU/UN sanctions, AML customer-due-diligence obligations, and the requirement that all cash payments exceeding EUR 2,500 be settled through a credit institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg has no export-proceeds surrender rules and imposes no mandatory conversion ratios. Export/API revenue held in foreign currency may be retained freely. However, BCL Regulation 2017/01 and CSSF reporting obligations require resident companies (including SCsps) to report cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 500,000 (or equivalent) for balance-of-payments statistical purposes within a defined calendar month. Failure to report may result in administrative fines, but no surrender or conversion of foreign currency is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dual account structure: Capital Escrow Account (EUR) + Operational Current Account (EUR/USD)
Capital Escrow Account (EUR) + Corporate Transaction Account (multi-currency)
Corporate Escrow Account + Operational Account with SWIFT and SEPA access
Partnership Capital Contribution Account + Active Treasury Account (EUR and foreign currency)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High. A Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under PSD2 may offer full IBAN, SEPA and SWIFT access, making it viable as a treasury gateway. However, a pure offshore EMI without a Luxembourg/EU licence cannot be used as a primary settlement bank because the CSSF requires payment institutions to be authorised in an EU/EEA state. Additionally, the target payment rail of USDC/USD can only be integrated through a CSSF-registered Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP), because under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004, as amended by the Law of 15 August 2019, any entity engaging in virtual-asset custody, exchange or transfer is subject to a VASP licence. Therefore, the recommended fintech stack is: (1) a Luxembourg-licensed EMI for fiat SEPA/SWIFT, (2) a CSSF-registered VASP for regulated USDC conversion, and (3) an internal record-keeping system that maps each digital wallet to a legal entity and invoice.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Luxembourg law (LFS Article 3-1 and CSSF Regulation 12-02), remote client onboarding is legally possible only if the bank applies qualified electronic identification (eIDAS QES) and a CSSF-accepted video procedure. In practice, tier-1 commercial banks require at least one in-person meeting at their Luxembourg office for the authorised signatories of an SCSp, particularly when the general partner is a non-resident legal entity or when the SCSp displays a blockchain/cryptocurrency-linked revenue stream. Therefore, a physical appearance of at least one director/manager is strongly recommended for the initial board-approved bank that will serve as the main clearing bank; for secondary banks, remote signing with notarised powers of attorney may be accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp capital is sourced from non-resident partners in high-risk jurisdictions or from crypto-exit proceeds, which may trigger enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete source-of-funds pack for each partner: notarised deed of contribution, bank statement showing the origin of the funds, a certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société), the RCS Luxembourg extract, the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract, a legal opinion from a Luxembourg notary, and a brief business plan demonstrating that the capital injection is a genuine equity contribution to a data-infrastructure venture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue attributable to 'public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways' may be construed as sensitive under GDPR / data-protection law, leading to customs or banking compliance red flags on cross-border data flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A GDPR-compliant processing records set (Article 30 of Regulation 2016/679), a data controller entity mapping, privacy policy, data-retention chart, contractual clauses with end customers confirming lawful scraping, and a technical architecture statement showing that no personal data of Luxembourg residents is captured without lawful basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payments through USDC and other cryptos may deter banks that lack a VASP-compliant interface or that have risk-aversion policies regarding speculative digital assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A compliance control narrative showing that all USDC receipts are channelled through a CSSF-licensed VASP, that counterparty wallets are screened against OFAC/EU sanctions lists in real time, that funds are converted to EUR within 1 business day, and that each on-chain transaction is logged with the transaction hash and legal business reference in the treasury ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound partner capital contributions must be transferred by SEPA or SWIFT to the SCSp's dedicated EUR escrow account maintained with a Luxembourg/EU bank. Payment reference must clearly state: (1) the SCSp commercial name and RCS number (e.g., 'RCS Luxembourg BXXXXX'), (2) the purpose of payment as 'Capital Contribution to SCSp', and (3) an appropriate BCL balance-of-payments code (e.g., 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital'). For USD injections, use SWIFT MT103 field 70 to include the same description and ensure that the converting bank is an EU-authorized institution. Any cash component above EUR 2,500 is unlawful. The bank must conduct a source-of-funds verification and record the transaction in the BCL statistical report (Form PROC/IT) when the value exceeds EUR 500,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements (e.g., server infrastructure, bandwidth, proxy IP licensing fees) must be cleared through the corporate account using SWIFT MT103 (for cross-border non-EUR payments) or SEPA Instant/SEPA Direct Debit (for EUR payments within the SEPA zone). For supplier financing, a commercially accepted method is an Import/Export Letter of Credit (UCP 600) opened by the Luxembourg bank in favour of the vendor; the SCSp must provide the purchase contract, a pro-forma invoice, and an insurance certificate. For smaller recurring API vendor fees, card rails (Visa/Mastercard) through the linked EMI are permissible. USDC outbound payments, if required by vendors, must be executed only via a CSSF-registered VASP, and each transfer must be accompanied by a treasury file containing the invoice ID, the wallet address, and the smart-contract hash.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) with an EU- or Luxembourg-authorised credit institution, subject to EMIR reporting when done bilaterally.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for less-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) permitted for trade-flow hedging, documented under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with a credit support annex.
FX swaps (short term up to 1 year) to cover temporally segregated EUR and USD liquidity positions, booked under a CSA or GMRA if collateralised.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) limited to committed facilities and hedges of the SCSp's long-term capex, executed only with a bank rated at least A- by Standard & Poor's.

European-style currency options for premium-based risk management, permitted only when purchased with full premium payment upfront, not when written (sold) by the SCSp unless the bank has separately approved a derivatives policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner information (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of the entity's initial RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 250–1,250 (approx. USD 270–1,350); potential daily default fines and forced compliance orders; repeated non-compliance may lead to suspension of filings or administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months from the financial year-end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000 (approx. USD 5,400); court order for compulsory filing; ultimate administrative strike-off from the RCS after repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority – ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months from the financial year-end; extensions to 31 December available upon timely request by a tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000; criminal sanctions for deliberate omission; escalation to attachment of assets or dissolution proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SCSp is subject to mandatory statutory audit if it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total balance-sheet assets EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average 50 employees during the financial year. Audit is also compulsory if the entity is a public-interest entity, part of a consolidated group obliged to prepare consolidated accounts, or operates as a regulated investment fund under CSSF supervision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is voluntarily permitted for individual accounts and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp's general partner or authorised manager must log into the RBE online portal before the registration anniversary and confirm that the beneficial owner information remains accurate. If the existing data is incorrect, an updated form F must be submitted in the same session; the confirmation is complete only when the RBE issues an electronic acknowledgement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (register des parts sociales)
Register of Beneficial Owners (internal, retrievable on demand)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 650 – 2,200 per year depending on the service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 15,000 depending on entity size, transaction volume, and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate maximum: 17% CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax at the Luxembourg City rate; effective CIT brackets are 15% up to EUR 175,000 and 17% above, excluding the municipal surcharge). An SCSp is fiscally transparent under Art. 175 LIR: the partnership itself pays no Luxembourg CIT, MBT, or net wealth tax; each partner is taxed directly on its distributive profit share. A non-resident corporate partner is subject to Luxembourg CIT only on Luxembourg-source profit attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax transparency pass-through: nil entity-level corporate income tax for the SCSp. IP box regime (80% exemption on net IP income) is unavailable to the transparent partnership, but an eligible corporate partner can apply it to its share. Luxembourg-resident corporate partners may use a 17-year CIT loss carryforward and an unlimited municipal business tax loss carryforward. No minimum capital tax for SCSp.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 / partnership income tax file (together with the annual corporate income tax return Form 621 for Luxembourg-resident corporate partners) filed via eCIT, the official RCD (Luxembourg Inland Revenue) electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year; financial statements to RCS within six months of year-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March following the tax year-end; RCD administrative practice automatically extends the filing deadline to 31 December of the following year for eCIT filers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Partner identification (FID number and full legal name)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The fiscal identification number and legal name of each general and limited partner owning a share in the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the non-resident partner’s home tax identification number and full legal name; if the partner is in a treaty jurisdiction, enter country code and confirm no Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / SCSp registered office and RCS registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg registered office, business address, and RCS/LEI details of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the exact Luxembourg registered office; a shell/letterbox address without substance will trigger the fatal red flags below.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Accounting period and balance sheet reference
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal period plus the balance sheet file reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the SCSp accounting period strictly with the calendar/tax year; non-resident partners relying on a foreign fiscal year must attach a reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the partnership taxable result (commercial web scraping API fee income minus expenses) among each partner by amount and percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The transparent SCSp files this schedule to notify Luxembourg source income; the non-resident corporate partner reports the same share on its home tax return and claims treaty relief if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If a Luxembourg-resident corporate partner is present, the share must be carried into Form 621 and the aggregate 24.94% headline rate applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Luxembourg permanent establishment and no Luxembourg-source income, mark 'no Luxembourg CIT exposure' but still file the informational return to avoid penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine between EUR 250 and EUR 2,500; for intentional non-filing the fine may rise to EUR 15,000. Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month on the unpaid CIT balance. Criminal tax fraud sanctions apply for deliberately omitting API revenue (see red flags).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% is the Luxembourg domestic dividend withholding tax rate applying to deemed qualifying distributions; however, because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, a profit distribution is not treated as a dividend as long as the SCSp does not opt into full CIT taxation. If an SCSp is nonetheless treated as a Luxembourg tax-resident corporation in the hands of the partner, the statutory 15% WHT may apply, subject to treaty relief and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% for a qualifying EU/EEA corporate partner holding at least 10% for 12 months).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must submit a Luxembourg withholding tax exemption/certificate request via the eTax/eCIT system before distribution, attaching: (i) a valid Luxembourg Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) of the recipient in the treaty counterparty; (ii) a completed Luxembourg dividend WHT reduction/refund form; (iii) evidence of beneficial ownership; and (iv) a shareholding percentage and holding-period declaration. Where WHT is withheld at the 15% statutory rate, the partner files an income tax refund claim with the Luxembourg tax authorities within the statute of limitations; for transparent SCSp structures there is no tax at source and no refund protocol is needed because the partner is taxed at personal/corporate level under the applicable treaty business-profits article.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic WHT 15% on Luxembourg-source royalties (only if the SCSp is deemed taxable and royalty is sourced in Luxembourg); most Luxembourg income tax treaties reduce royalty WHT to 0%, and the EU Interest-Royalty Directive provides 0% for qualifying associated companies. Interest: Luxembourg does not levy a general withholding tax on debt interest paid by an SCSp; the vast majority of DTA protocols provide a 0% to 10% rate for portfolio interest, and the EU Interest-Royalty Directive grants 0% for 25%+ corporate shareholders held for 24 months.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 450,000 in aggregate controlled related-party transactions mandating a Luxembourg Local File and Master File under the Luxembourg transfer-pricing documentation rules; if the related party is resident in a non-cooperative jurisdiction, the threshold is EUR 100,000 per transaction or aggregate exposure above EUR 450,000, and a contemporaneous benchmarking study must be kept. For the public commercial web scraping API business, the arm's-length gross margin on API gateway access and revenue-sharing data resale must be documented.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not enact a separate Economic Substance Regulation; substance requirements are embedded in the ATAD general anti-abuse rule (Art. 6 LIR), the abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. 56 LIR), and the OECD/G20 BEPS standards. An SCSp deriving EUR-scale API commercial income must maintain real substance: Luxembourg office premises, local qualified management and technical staff, board decisions made in Luxembourg, and an active bank account. Corporate partners and directors must justify the SCSp as a genuine commercial venture, not a shell conduit, to avoid reclassification and denial of treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and deliberate filing omissions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting web scraping API revenue from the SCSp informational return and filing false partner allocation schedules to understate the Luxembourg-resident corporate partner’s taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at the full 24.94% aggregate rate; a tax fraud fine of EUR 250 to EUR 50,000; late payment interest at 0.6% per month; and under Art. 397 LIR, imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years for wilful tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner’s director who signs false schedules faces joint and several civil liability for the unpaid CIT, plus criminal prosecution under Art. 397 LIR, a travel ban and asset freeze under the Luxembourg General Tax Code collection measures, and disqualification as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / artificial arrangement / substance abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp operating as a letterbox entity: no employees, no physical office, nominee limited partners, and routing of API fees through a zero-tax jurisdiction to a Luxembourg corporate taxpayer without legitimate commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp under Art. 56 LIR (abuse of law); the profit is re-attributed to the Luxembourg principal; a 10% abuse penalty; denial of treaty benefits under the OECD principal-purpose test; and a EUR 250,000 penalty under DAC 6 for failure to disclose the reportable cross-border arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for tax restitutions, subject to criminal penalties for aiding tax avoidance, a 5-year imprisonment risk under money-laundering provisions if assets are concealed, and an individual travel ban in summary tax collection proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a controlled Swiss/DE platform below the arm's-length price for data management or an excessive profit split on the API gateway (e.g., EUR 1.2 million charged where CUP indicates EUR 3 million).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment under Art. 56(3) LIR; secondary cash adjustment; a penalty of 10% of the upward adjustment; late interest at 0.6% per month; and disallowance of any non-arm's-length expense paid to the SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signed the intercompany agreements bears personal civil liability for the additional tax if the SCSp is insolvent, and criminal charges apply for preparing false transfer-pricing documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp accepts USDC cryptocurrency payments and Stripe card revenue without performing customer due diligence or identifying the ultimate beneficial owner of the limited partners; false or incomplete Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended), fines up to EUR 5 million and imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years; the RBE regime imposes administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 for non-filing or false BO declarations; the Luxembourg CSSF can impose a separate enforcement penalty if the payment activity requires a payment institution license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability for AML breaches, personal fines, removal from the board, travel bans, and seizure of assets involved in the money laundering chain; using an unlicensed payment flow can also trigger prohibition orders against the directors.
